q: Who counts the tugboat fuel when our ship berths at a port?
title: Tugboat fuel at berthing: whose scope
short: The tug operator burns the fuel, so it is their Scope 1. For a shipping line it is a bought service, Scope 3. For an exporter it usually sits inside the freight emissions your carrier or forwarder reports. Count it once, at the level of the freight figure.
audience: Shipping lines, port users and exporters

ul: Tug owner: Scope 1, from the diesel it burns.
Port that runs its own tugs: Scope 1.
Shipping line hiring tugs: Scope 3 purchased services.
Exporter: inside the sea freight figure, not a separate line.

p: If your forwarder's report already uses a well-to-wake figure per container, do not add port services again on top.

senseible: Senseible reads bills, fuel invoices and production records into dated, fingerprinted records, so the figure you send a buyer can be traced to its documents.
